newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in nervous trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.02 percent to close at 1.0390 per dollar on the commercial foreign exchange market as players again speculated nervously on dollar inflows and outflows, dealers said.
The real was bought and sold at between 1.0380 and 1.0395 per dollar in volatile trade in the morning.
But the market calmed down some in the afternoon after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0375 to 1.0425 per dollar through a buy/sell auction, dealers said.
The previous one was set on December 10 between 1.0360 and 1.0410 reais to the dollar.
Dealers said dollar inflows and outflows will continue to be decisive in coming days in determining the trade level for the local currency.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real dropped 0.1 percent to close at 1.0430 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended at 1.130 per greenback, 1.16 percent down, mostly due to a reduction in the supply of dollars.
